name: Coffee Pub Showrunner
tagline: Feed OBS the sources, audio, video and metadata for a streamed game.
pitch: A desktop app that gets your game, your players and your cues into OBS, and keeps them there. OBS still does the streaming and recording; Showrunner does the setup and the cueing.
description: A standalone macOS and Windows app that wraps any web page in a fixed-size window so OBS can capture it as its own source, keeps those sources cropped, pointed and in sync, and lets Foundry modules cue OBS actions.

downloads.label: Download for Windows
downloads.note: We tested Windows on real hardware with an earlier release and it worked. We have not yet re-checked 0.3.2 on Windows. Check the known issues page if a window misbehaves.

features.title: Clean window capture
features.text: Borderless windows with a slim bar of their own, sized to the exact pixels you set. Linked OBS sources crop the bar away, so OBS sees only the page.

features.title: Sources that stay put
features.text: Stable window names keep OBS pointed at the right window after every launch, so you never re-pick a window. Rendering is never throttled behind other windows.

features.title: Named regions
features.text: Draw a rectangle on a snapshot, or name a CSS selector, and Showrunner creates a cropped OBS source and keeps the crop current.

features.title: Players as sources
features.text: Sign in to your party's voice and video server and publish each player as their own OBS Browser Source with one click.

features.title: Automations
features.text: Foundry modules such as Herald can report that combat started or a scene changed, and a rule turns that into an OBS action: switch scene, show or hide a source, start or stop recording or streaming.

features.title: Edge dock
features.text: Park windows under a slim strip at the screen edge to get them out of the way while OBS keeps capturing them. Hover for thumbnails, with Start, Stop and Sync shortcuts.

features.title: Session groups
features.text: Windows in the same group share one login, so you sign in once. Windows in different groups stay separate.

features.title: YouTube upload
features.text: Optionally upload the finished recording to your own YouTube channel, with the title and description you set for the session. Off until you connect your own Google Cloud project.

steps: Download the installer for your computer from the latest release and open it. The builds are not code-signed, so macOS and Windows each show a one-time warning.
Open the control panel, add a window (up to five) with a label and a URL, such as your game canvas and a stream-facing view.
Connect to OBS from the Session tab so Showrunner creates the sources and keeps them pointed at your windows.
needs: macOS 12 or newer (Apple Silicon or Intel), or Windows 10 or newer (x64)
firstLaunch: macOS: right-click the app in Applications, choose Open, then Open again in the dialog.
Windows: when SmartScreen says Windows protected your PC, click More info, then Run anyway.

gallery.title: The scene, wired up
gallery.text: This is an OBS scene after Showrunner has set it up: the live game, two regions and the players all arrive as sources. there is nothing to pick or crop by hand.
gallery.caption: Showrunner keeps the OBS scene wired up: the live game, regions and players as sources.

gallery.title: One window, one source
gallery.text: Each page you want on stream gets its own window with an exact size, a session group and launch options. OBS captures the page without the title bar, so what you set is what viewers see.
gallery.caption: Each app window is its own OBS source.

gallery.title: Split a window up
gallery.text: You can cut a window into regions, either by drawing a rectangle or by naming a CSS selector. A chat feed or a stats panel then becomes its own OBS source that you can place anywhere in a scene.
gallery.caption: Split a window into regions, each its own OBS source.

gallery.title: Players in one click
gallery.text: Once you're signed in to Chameleon, your room's members and participants are listed here. One click adds a player to OBS as a source, so you're not building player tiles by hand.
gallery.caption: Chameleon: your room, members and participants, ready to add to OBS.

gallery.title: Everything at a glance
gallery.text: The Configuration tab shows whether OBS, Chameleon, Automations and YouTube are connected, and has the recording, streaming and scene controls. You can run a session from one panel.
gallery.caption: Connections, OBS controls and scenes at a glance.

gallery.title: The edge dock
gallery.text: The dock keeps your windows parked at the screen edge while OBS keeps capturing them. You can hover for the recording and live timers, the current scene and a thumbnail of each window.
gallery.caption: The edge dock: hover for REC and LIVE timers, the current scene and a thumbnail of every window.

gallery.title: Cues and uploads
gallery.text: Foundry modules can send events that a rule turns into an OBS action, and finished recordings can upload to your own YouTube channel. You set both up once, and then they run from your rule sets.
gallery.caption: Automations server and YouTube upload, set up once and used by rule sets.

note: Coffee Pub Showrunner is free to download and use for now. It is proprietary, not open source: you can read the source, but you can't copy, redistribute or resell it. A later version may be paid, but a version you have already downloaded stays usable. We tested Windows on real hardware with an earlier release and it worked, but We have not yet re-checked 0.3.2 there, so check the Known issues page if a window misbehaves. This is a personal project, so back up your OBS profile before trying anything new.
